name: Titanium.UI.ImageView
summary: A view to display a single image or series of animated images.
description:
Use the [Titanium.UI.createImageView](api:Titanium.UI#createImageView) method or **`<ImageView>`** Alloy element to create an `ImageView`.

Specifying either a `width` or `height` property for this view will scale its image(s) with
the aspect ratio maintained, up to a maximum size that does not exceed its parent view.

#### Remote Images

You can display both local and remote images in an ImageView. When loading remote images, you should
set the defaultImage property to a local image, which will be displayed while the remote image is being
downloaded. Remote images are cached automatically on the iOS-, Android- and Windows platform.

Android Note: Android 6 and later uses runtime permissions to secure the user's privacy.
Therefore, you should call [Titanium.Filesystem.requestStoragePermissions](api:Titanium.Filesystem#requestStoragePermissions) before attempting to load remote images.

Read more about remote images and general best practices in the [Image Best Practices Guide](https://titaniumsdk.com/guide/Titanium_SDK/Titanium_SDK_Guide/Best_Practices_and_Recommendations/Image_Best_Practices.html#caching-remote-images).

#### Android 9-Patch Scaled Images

A nine-patch (9-patch) image is simply a standard `png` image with a transparent border of a
single pixel, containing "guides" defined by solid black (`#000`) color fills. Guides added to the
top and left edges determine that the image may be stretched in horizontal and vertical planes
respectively. Optionally, the content area may be defined by guides added to the bottom and
right edges.

Although any image editor may be used to create the guides, certain settings can cause the edges
of the graphic to "bleed" into the transparent border, consequently making it non-transparent.
Thus, the `draw9patch` utility provided in the Android SDK tools directory is recommended for
this purpose.

For further information about nine-patch images and the Android utility, see the
[Nine-patch](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/graphics/drawables#nine-patch)
and [Draw 9-patch](https://developer.android.com/studio/write/draw9patch) sections
of the Android Developer website.

The nine-patch technique may be used with any of Titanium's static image properties. See the
"Button with Nine-patch Background Image" example for a demonstration.

examples.title: Basic Image View
Button with Nine-patch Background Image
Alloy XML Markup
examples.code:
Previous basic image view example as an Alloy view.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <Window id="win" backgroundColor="white">
        <ImageView id="image" image="/images/myimage.png" />
    </Window>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: animating
properties.summary: Indicates whether animation is running.
properties.default: false on creation, true on load (Android), false (iPhone, iPad)

properties.name: autorotate
properties.summary:
Indicates whether the image should be rotated based on EXIF orientation data.

Before Titanium 10.1.0, this defaulted to `false` on Android.

properties.name: decodeRetries
properties.summary: Number of times to retry decoding the bitmap at a URL.
properties.description: Defaults to 2 on Titanium 10.1.0 and higher. Defaults to 5 on older SDK versions.

properties.name: defaultImage
properties.summary: Local path to the default image to display while loading a remote image.

properties.name: duration
properties.summary: Amount of time in milliseconds to animate one cycle.
properties.description:
Starting with release 2.1.1, the minimum duration is 30 ms and the default duration is 200 ms.

On Android, prior to release 2.1.1, if any images are assigned to the `images` property when the animation is
started, duration will be set to the number of images multiplied by 33 ms. If no images
are assigned, duration will be set to 100 ms.

On iOS, prior to release 2.1.1, the default is 30 ms.

On Android, if the value of duration is changed, [stop](api:Titanium.UI.ImageView#stop)
and [start](api:Titanium.UI.ImageView#start) need to be called for the new value to take effect.
properties.default: 200 ms in Release 2.1.1 and later. Platform-specific default in earlier releases.

properties.name: enableZoomControls
properties.summary: Show zoom controls when the user touches the image view.

properties.name: hires
properties.summary:
Set to `true` to prevent scaling of 2x/3x-resolution remote images for retina
displays.
properties.description:
Causes images to display at 50%, where one pixel of the graphic maps to one physical pixel
on-screen. This functionality is automatically determined for local images via their
filenames, and thus this property is only applicable to remote images.

properties.name: image
properties.summary: Image to display.
properties.description:
Image to display, defined using a local filesystem path, a `File` object, a remote URL,
or a `Blob` object containing image data.

For Android, if there is a redirect and change in protocol, it will not follow. For example,
from http to https and vice versa. See [Java Bug Database](http://bugs.java.com/bugdatabase/view_bug.do?bug_id=4620571)
for more information.

properties.name: images
properties.summary:
Array of images to animate, defined using local filesystem paths, `File` objects,
remote URLs (Android only), or `Blob` objects containing image data.

When using this property, an initial `start()` needs to be called upon the ImageView before any image will show in this imageview.

Related properties/methods to look at: `start`, `stop`, `pause`, `reverse`, `resume` and `repeatCount`

properties.name: imageTouchFeedback
properties.summary: Enables a ripple effect when the foreground image is touched.
properties.description:
Note that the [touchFeedback](api:Titanium.UI.View#touchFeedback) property applies a ripple effect to the
view's background. If the image is opaque and completely covers the view (such as a photo),
then the background's ripple won't be visible. In this case, you should use this `imageTouchFeedback`
property to apply a ripple effect to the foreground image assigned via the `image` property.

properties.name: imageTouchFeedbackColor
properties.summary: Optional touch feedback ripple color. This has no effect unless `imageTouchFeedback` is true.

properties.name: paused
properties.summary: Indicates whether the animation is paused.

properties.name: preventDefaultImage
properties.summary:
Prevent the default image from being displayed while loading a remote image. This property
is ignored when the `defaultImage` property is set.

properties.name: repeatCount
properties.summary: Number of times to repeat the image animation.

properties.name: reverse
properties.summary: Run the animation in reverse.

properties.name: scalingMode
properties.summary: Determines how the image is scaled within the view.

properties.name: tintColor
properties.summary: The view's tintColor. Android does not support setting instances of [Titanium.UI.Color](api:Titanium.UI.Color)

methods.name: addSymbolEffect
methods.summary: Adds a symbol effect to the image view with specified options, animation, and callback.

parameters.name: symbolEffect
parameters.summary: The symbol effect to add. One of `pulse`, `bounce`, `appear`, `disappear`, `variableColor` or `scale`.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: The options for the symbol effect. One of `repeating`, `nonRepeating`, `repeatCount` or `speed`.

parameters.name: animated
parameters.summary: A Boolean value that indicates whether to animate the addition of a `scale`, `appear`, or `disappear` effect.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary: A callback the system calls after the effect’s addition is complete.

methods.name: pause
methods.summary: Pauses a running animation. Use `resume` method to continue.
methods.description: This method only works if multiple images are specified.

methods.name: resume
methods.summary: Resumes an animation from a `pause` state.
methods.description: This method only works if multiple images are specified.

methods.name: start
methods.summary: Starts the image animation. On Android, also resets `index` to the first image.
methods.description: This method only works if multiple images are specified.

methods.name: stop
methods.summary: Stops a running animation. On iOS, also resets `index` to the first image.
methods.description: This method only works if multiple images are specified.

methods.name: toBlob
methods.summary: Returns the image as a Blob object.

events.name: change
events.summary: Fired for each frame change during an animation.

properties.name: index
properties.summary: Index of the image frame being displayed.

events.name: error
events.summary: Fired when an image fails to load.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates a successful operation. Returns `false`.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned. May be undefined.

properties.name: code
properties.summary:
Error code.
If the error was generated by the operating system, that system's error value
is used. Otherwise, this value will be -1.

properties.name: image
properties.summary: URL of the image that failed to load.

events.name: load
events.summary: Fired when either the initial image and/or all of the images in an animation are loaded.

properties.name: state
properties.summary:
Set to `image` when the image defined in the [image](api:Titanium.UI.ImageView#image)
property is loaded. Set to `images`, when the series of images defined in the
[images](api:Titanium.UI.ImageView#images) property are loaded.
